target.title: fix(agent): classify stuck recovery as idle timeout
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Fixes #93610. Diagnostic stuck-session recovery aborted active embedded runs with the same downstream semantics as user/restart/superseded aborts, so failover could see an external abort and surface `Request was aborted` instead of using the configured idle-timeout fallback path.
- Why it matters / User impact: Cron/provider sessions that stall while a model call is actively in flight can use the existing idle-timeout rotate/fallback path, while stale post-model recoveries and side-effecting tool stalls stay out of automatic replay paths.
- Solution: Preserve `stuck_recovery` through diagnostic abort/drain and reply-run propagation, preserve the existing reply-run abortability guard for stuck recovery, then classify replay safety from active model-call state and active potential-side-effect tool state before failover observes abort semantics.
- Current-head refresh: after ClawSweeper's latest reviews, added the missing reply-run abortability guard for stuck recovery, fixed the OpenAI chat tools response-body timeout/cancel race so timeout errors are not masked as clean EOF, and re-ran production-module runtime proof, ClawSweeper acceptance tests, focused Vitest shards, changed-file oxlint, and whitespace check against exact committed head `3402c08a37b9092ae5dda8919edcedc5d559deda`.
- Fixes #93610

## What Problem This Solves

Diagnostic stuck-session recovery needs different downstream semantics depending on what was active when recovery fired. A stalled model call can safely use the existing idle-timeout fallback path; an active potential-side-effect tool call must not be replayed; stale or unknown recovery should remain external-abort-like.

## User Impact

Users running scheduled or provider-backed embedded-agent sessions get a safer recovery path when the stuck-session watchdog interrupts an active model call. The patch avoids widening retry behavior for side-effecting tool execution, so recovery does not silently replay operations that may already have touched external state.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent downstream recovery classification hardening. Provider-boundary PRs such as #93965 are related to the original opencode-go stream outage, but this PR covers the generic downstream diagnostic recovery and failover-classification boundary.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **#93965:** Provider-owned opencode-go stream guard. It addresses the upstream provider stream boundary and formally closed the original issue. This PR does not replace it.
- **#93640:** Earlier provider-scoped stalled stream guard. It overlaps the provider-boundary direction and remains separate from this downstream recovery classification boundary.
- **#98580:** Adjacent timeout-budget work for cron stuck recovery. Landing order should be deliberate because it can affect when recovery fires, but this PR still owns what happens after diagnostic recovery aborts an active embedded run.
- **This PR:** Downstream embedded-run recovery safety. It fixes the boundary after diagnostic stuck-session recovery aborts an active embedded run: `stuck_recovery` must survive registry/reply-run propagation, and replay safety must be classified before failover decides whether retry/fallback is allowed.
- **Why this can still land alongside provider/timeout-budget fixes:** Even with provider-owned stream termination guards or timeout-budget changes, the generic stuck-session recovery path still needs replay-safe semantics for model stalls, side-effecting tool stalls, and stale recovery.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:**
```text
Diagnostic stuck-session recovery preserves `stuck_recovery` through embedded-run and reply-run boundaries, then classifies replay safety before failover observes abort semantics:
- active model-call stall with no active potential-side-effect tool => model_idle_timeout, eligible for the existing rotate/fallback path;
- active side-effecting tool stall => tool_execution_timeout, not idle timeout, so failover does not replay side effects;
- stale post-model / pre-model / unknown stuck recovery => external_abort, not a replay path.
```

A production-module runtime probe imported the same stuck-recovery classifier, embedded-run registry, abort/drain path, and reply-run registry modules from this worktree. It registered an in-process active embedded run, aborted it with `abortReason: "stuck_recovery"`, waited for drain, and separately exercised reply-run stuck-recovery cancellation.

- **Observed result after fix:**
```text
The current-head production-module runtime probe observed the intended downstream behavior:
- model-call stuck recovery classified as model_idle_timeout;
- active side-effecting tool stuck recovery classified as tool_execution_timeout;
- stale or unknown stuck recovery classified as external_abort;
- abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun forwarded abortReason=stuck_recovery to the active embedded-run handle and drained without force clear;
- reply-run abort propagation preserved stuck_recovery and produced aborted_for_stuck_recovery;
- non-abortable reply operations now reject stuck-recovery aborts when a terminal retained failure already exists or when the attached backend is finalizing, leaving result state intact and avoiding backend cancel.
- OpenAI chat-tools response body timeouts now reject with `chat completions request timed out after 1s` before reader cancellation can be mistaken for clean EOF, and the regression does not enter the `non-JSON response` path.

The focused tests also pass across reply-run fallback, reply-run abortability guards, stuck-recovery classifier/registry, active model-call lifecycle, active tool side-effect boundaries, diagnostic recovery runtime, OpenAI chat-tools timeout cleanup, and the current conflict-resolution seams.
```

The fresh proof exercises the downstream OpenClaw diagnostic recovery and failover-classification boundary on the current PR head. Provider-owned stream termination behavior remains covered by provider-boundary PRs and is not claimed as live provider proof here.
```

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix for the downstream diagnostic recovery / embedded-run failover classification boundary; complementary to provider-owned stream guard fixes.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 — runtime/live classification proof:** Addressed with current-head production-module runtime proof showing model-call stuck recovery => `model_idle_timeout`, side-effecting tool stuck recovery => `tool_execution_timeout`, and stale/unknown recovery => `external_abort`.
- **RF-002 — owner replay-safety confirmation:** Contributor proof is supplied, but final agent/session-owner sign-off remains a maintainer decision before merge.
- **RF-003 — after-fix real behavior proof:** Addressed with terminal runtime-harness output in `current-head-stuck-recovery-runtime-proof-20260704-3402c08.json`, plus current-head focused tests.
- **RF-004 — intentional session recovery semantic change:** Disclosed as intentional and bounded: only active model-call stalls without active potential-side-effect tools enter model idle-timeout fallback semantics.
- **RF-005 — active side-effect counter boundary:** Covered by focused tests and runtime classification; final owner confirmation of the exact replay-safety boundary remains a maintainer decision.
- **RF-006 — original opencode-go outage proof gap:** Disclosed explicitly. This PR proves the downstream recovery boundary; it does not claim a live opencode-go provider outage reproduction.
- **RF-007 — adjacent #98580 timeout-budget work:** Disclosed in the linked PR analysis. That work can affect when recovery fires; this PR owns how recovery is classified after it fires.
- **RF-008 — current-head exact proof:** Addressed with fresh runtime proof, focused verification, changed-file oxlint, and diff check after the latest code repair; the verification marker binds exact committed head `3402c08a37b9092ae5dda8919edcedc5d559deda` with an empty pending diff.
- **RF-009 — focused current-head test group:** Addressed by `current-head-focused-vitest-20260704-3402c08.log`, passing 6 shards / 573 tests.
- **RF-010 — stuck recovery / failover / tool / diagnostic test group:** Included in the same focused suite and passed on current head.
- **RF-011 — maintainer comment about stuck phase classification:** Addressed by classifying the stuck phase before abort semantics reach failover: active model-call, active side-effecting tool, and stale/unknown recovery now remain distinct.
- **RF-012 — preserve reply-run abortability for stuck recovery:** Addressed by adding the existing `isReplyOperationAbortable(operation)` guard to `abortForStuckRecovery()` in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.ts`, plus focused coverage proving retained terminal failures and finalizing non-abortable backends reject stuck-recovery aborts without cancelling the backend.
- **RF-013 — preserve OpenAI chat-tools timeout errors:** Addressed by making response-body timeout handling reject immediately and cancel the reader fire-and-forget in `scripts/e2e/lib/openai-chat-tools/client.mjs`, plus E2E coverage proving a timed-out body read reports `chat completions request timed out after 1s` and does not fall through to the `non-JSON response` path.

## CI attribution

Before this narrow RF-013 repair, the previous remote PR head had no visible failed or pending checks in daily-fix final status:

```text
FAIL 0 / PENDING 0 / PASS 67 / SKIPPED 33
mergeable=MERGEABLE mergeStateStatus=CLEAN
ClawSweeper blocker before this patch: status: waiting on author for the OpenAI chat-tools timeout/cancel race
```

The new exact committed head `3402c08a37b9092ae5dda8919edcedc5d559deda` has fresh local verification recorded above and will rely on the normal pull_request checks after push. An earlier `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` socket-close timeout was attributed as non-PR-introduced flaky/rerun-only and was not addressed with unrelated tooling/release-check changes.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/openai-compatible-chat-tools.e2e.test.ts`.
- **Target test files:** `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/openai-compatible-chat-tools.e2e.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/stuck-recovery-abort.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-policy.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`, `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts`, `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`, and `src/flows/channel-setup.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Diagnostic stuck recovery carries `abortReason: "stuck_recovery"`; active model-call stalls are replay-safe idle timeouts only while a model call is active and no active potential-side-effect tool execution exists; side-effecting tool stalls are classified as tool-execution timeouts and do not trigger automatic fallback/retry; stale post-model or unknown recovery remains external-abort-like; reply-run stuck recovery preserves the same abortability invariant as user/restart aborts for retained terminal failures and finalizing non-abortable backends; OpenAI chat-tools response-body timeouts reject with the timeout error before reader cancellation can be observed as clean EOF.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The bug is at the abort-classification/reply-run abortability boundary between diagnostic recovery and embedded attempt failover, plus the E2E OpenAI chat-tools response-body timeout cleanup path called out by ClawSweeper. The tests cover the classifier, active model-call lifecycle, active tool side-effect signal, diagnostic recovery, registry abort/drain reason propagation, reply-run stuck-recovery propagation, non-abortable reply operation guards, timed-out body-read error propagation, and the current-main merge-conflict seams without changing public provider behavior.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** session-state, availability, message-delivery, and security-boundary.
- **Risk explanation:** The diff touches active embedded-run abort classification, diagnostic model-call lifecycle bookkeeping, reply-run cancellation reasons and abortability, active potential-side-effect tool tracking, and test fixtures near channel setup / doctor-health flows. Incorrect classification could affect session cleanup, user/restart/superseded aborts, timeout retry/fallback behavior, message delivery test seams, finalizing reply lifecycle state, or side-effecting tool replay safety.
- **Why acceptable:** The patch does not relax failover policy or replay all stuck recoveries. It narrows classification at the internal owner boundary where diagnostic recovery, embedded-run state, active model calls, active tool replay-safety state, and reply-run abortability are available; user/restart/superseded abort behavior remains external-abort-like; side-effecting tools and non-abortable reply operations remain out of automatic fallback/retry; current-head runtime proof and focused regression tests cover the risk seams.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Risk labels considered:** session-state and availability.
- **Why acceptable:** The patch does not change provider wire format, model routing, public config, persisted schema, or fallback policy. It narrows abort semantics at the internal owner boundary where diagnostic recovery, embedded-run state, active model calls, active tool replay-safety state, and reply-run abortability are available.
- **Compatibility:** Existing `user_abort`, `restart`, and `superseded` semantics remain external-abort-like. The existing failover policy remains the source of truth for whether model idle timeouts rotate/fallback and for keeping tool-execution timeouts out of replay paths. Stuck recovery now uses the same reply-run abortability guard as user/restart aborts for non-abortable reply operations.

## Public contract review

- **Contract surface:** Internal embedded-run abort reason plumbing, diagnostic model-call observation lifecycle, attempt-local recovery classification, active tool replay-safety state, reply-run stuck-recovery cancellation, and tooling test-client timeout cleanup only.
- **Related open PR scan:** #93965 and #93640 cover provider-boundary stream handling. #98580 covers adjacent cron stuck-recovery timeout-budget behavior. This PR does not alter public API, protocol, config, schema, provider catalog, model defaults, gateway config, or provider wire/data format.
- **Compatibility / default behavior:** Existing `user_abort`, `restart`, and `superseded` semantics remain external-abort-like. Existing failover policy remains unchanged; this PR only maps `stuck_recovery` to model idle-timeout semantics when the active phase is a model call and no active potential-side-effect tool is in flight, and it preserves the existing reply-run abortability guard for non-abortable operations.
- **Out of scope:** Live provider transport behavior, opencode-go SSE parsing, fallback model selection policy, cron scheduler timeout policy, channel delivery semantics, plugin contracts, public config, persisted schema, and broader tool replay-policy changes are intentionally unchanged.

## What was not changed

- No provider stream parser changes.
- No opencode-go payload wrapper changes.
- No model routing, fallback selection, gateway protocol, or public config changes.
- No channel delivery or plugin contract changes.
- No persisted data model or migration changes.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The source defect was an abort-classification contract violation between diagnostic stuck-session recovery and embedded attempt failover. Diagnostic recovery knew it was reclaiming a stale internal run, but downstream classification could lose the internal `stuck_recovery` reason or treat recovered stuck runs too broadly as model idle timeouts.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix preserves `stuck_recovery` through diagnostic abort/drain and reply-run propagation, keeps stuck recovery behind the existing reply-run abortability guard, then classifies replay safety from active model-call and active potential-side-effect tool state before failover observes abort semantics. That keeps model-call fallback available without replaying side-effecting tool work or aborting finalizing reply operations that the reply lifecycle already treats as non-abortable.
- **Scope boundary:** The root-cause boundary is attempt-local classification after diagnostic recovery aborts an active embedded run. Provider parsing, opencode-go stream termination, model routing, fallback model selection, cron timeout budget, public config, gateway protocol, channel delivery, plugin contracts, and persisted schema are intentionally left unchanged.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** Source-of-truth ownership stays in diagnostic recovery, embedded run registry, attempt-local stuck-recovery classification, diagnostic model-call terminal events, and active tool replay-safety state. The fix classifies before failover observes abort semantics rather than adding downstream string checks or provider-specific special cases.
- **Patch quality notes:** The `scripts/e2e/lib/openai-chat-tools/client.mjs` cancellation catch is limited to test-client cleanup after timeout so response shutdown can finish without changing production provider parsing. The stuck-recovery retry/fallback behavior is not widened globally; the new classifier only treats active model-call stalls as model idle timeouts and gives active potential-side-effect tools precedence as tool-execution timeouts. The reply-run `stuck_recovery` return path preserves a distinct abort result instead of converting it to user/restart/superseded semantics, while using the same abortability guard as user/restart aborts for retained failures and finalizing backends.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the downstream recovery-classification boundary; maintainer/session-owner decision still required for replay-safety sign-off and landing order relative to adjacent provider/timeout-budget work.

## Summary

- Problem: Fixes #93610. Diagnostic stuck-session recovery aborted active embedded runs with the same downstream semantics as user/restart/superseded aborts, so failover could see an external abort and surface `Request was aborted` instead of using the configured idle-timeout fallback path.
- Why it matters / User impact: Cron/provider sessions that stall while a model call is actively in flight can use the existing idle-timeout rotate/fallback path, while stale post-model recoveries and side-effecting tool stalls stay out of automatic replay paths.
- Solution: Preserve `stuck_recovery` through diagnostic abort/drain and reply-run propagation, preserve the existing reply-run abortability guard for stuck recovery, then classify replay safety from active model-call state and active potential-side-effect tool state before failover observes abort semantics.
- Current-head refresh: after ClawSweeper's latest reviews, added the missing reply-run abortability guard for stuck recovery, fixed the OpenAI chat tools response-body timeout/cancel race so timeout errors are not masked as clean EOF, and re-ran production-module runtime proof, ClawSweeper acceptance tests, focused Vitest shards, changed-file oxlint, and whitespace check against exact committed head `3402c08a37b9092ae5dda8919edcedc5d559deda`.
- Fixes #93610

## What Problem This Solves

Diagnostic stuck-session recovery needs different downstream semantics depending on what was active when recovery fired. A stalled model call can safely use the existing idle-timeout fallback path; an active potential-side-effect tool call must not be replayed; stale or unknown recovery should remain external-abort-like.

## User Impact

Users running scheduled or provider-backed embedded-agent sessions get a safer recovery path when the stuck-session watchdog interrupts an active model call. The patch avoids widening retry behavior for side-effecting tool execution, so recovery does not silently replay operations that may already have touched external state.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent downstream recovery classification hardening. Provider-boundary PRs such as #93965 are related to the original opencode-go stream outage, but this PR covers the generic downstream diagnostic recovery and failover-classification boundary.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **#93965:** Provider-owned opencode-go stream guard. It addresses the upstream provider stream boundary and formally closed the original issue. This PR does not replace it.
- **#93640:** Earlier provider-scoped stalled stream guard. It overlaps the provider-boundary direction and remains separate from this downstream recovery classification boundary.
- **#98580:** Adjacent timeout-budget work for cron stuck recovery. Landing order should be deliberate because it can affect when recovery fires, but this PR still owns what happens after diagnostic recovery aborts an active embedded run.
- **This PR:** Downstream embedded-run recovery safety. It fixes the boundary after diagnostic stuck-session recovery aborts an active embedded run: `stuck_recovery` must survive registry/reply-run propagation, and replay safety must be classified before failover decides whether retry/fallback is allowed.
- **Why this can still land alongside provider/timeout-budget fixes:** Even with provider-owned stream termination guards or timeout-budget changes, the generic stuck-session recovery path still needs replay-safe semantics for model stalls, side-effecting tool stalls, and stale recovery.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:**
```text
Diagnostic stuck-session recovery preserves `stuck_recovery` through embedded-run and reply-run boundaries, then classifies replay safety before failover observes abort semantics:
- active model-call stall with no active potential-side-effect tool => model_idle_timeout, eligible for the existing rotate/fallback path;
- active side-effecting tool stall => tool_execution_timeout, not idle timeout, so failover does not replay side effects;
- stale post-model / pre-model / unknown stuck recovery => external_abort, not a replay path.
```
